newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African industrials end weaker, golds off.
newsitem.headline: S.African industrials end weaker, golds off.

text.p: South African shares ended Friday stunted in directionless trade with industrials gasping at lower levels and gold finishing weaker despite bullion's recent recoveries, dealers said.
They said sentiment in the industrials sector had continued to worsen after poor results from some of the market's key industrial companies.
The Industrial index finished down 19.4 points at 8,421.2, the gold index down 26.8 points at 1,228.3 and the all-share down 30.3 points at 7,142.8.

Dealers said gold shares which had been spiced up by bullion's attempts at a new life above $347 at the beginning of the week had suffered on Germany's plans to revalue its gold reserves in order to offset its budget deficit.
Bullion fell before the close from around $347 and was last bid at $344.20.
Dealers said market volumes had shrunk on Friday with around 549 million rand worth of shares traded by the close compared to Thursday's 772 million rand.

They said underlying market sentiment on the day had been negative and the trend was likely to continue next week amid a lack of fresh economic news and a dimmed outlook for an immediate interest rate cut.
